intended_scope: Substations, relays, breakers, transformers, control cabinets, utility boundaries, and operational communication context relevant to electric-power and utility operations, without attempting full power-system simulation or protection-engineering specification coverage.
measurement_signal_expectations: Breaker status, transformer health, relay evidence, and utility topology context should preserve event or quality timing semantics.
Time ordering is important for trip, suppression, and switching analysis.
event_alarm_expectations: Protective events, communication loss, alarm state, and suppression windows should remain explicit.
Operational alerts should remain distinct from later dispatch or work decisions.
reliability_work_requirements: Switching or maintenance work should remain linked to verification context.
Outage or service-impact outcomes should remain measurable rather than implied.

safety_cyber_applicability.safety_profile_applicability: Applicable where switching safety, lockout, or proof-test context must remain visible.
safety_cyber_applicability.cyber_profile_applicability: Strongly applicable for relay, PLC, and control-cabinet zone or conduit context.
notes: The profile does not attempt a complete electrical protection study model.
Cyber applicability is foundational and does not imply security-level or control-framework completeness.

servicenow_serving_projection_implicatio: Workflow projections should expose current operational state, outage risk, and relevant asset relationships.
Do not treat raw SCADA or relay event streams as workflow-primary records.
standards_mapping_applicability: ISA-95 or IEC 62264 where enterprise-control boundaries matter
known_exclusions: Detailed power-flow, contingency, or relay settings management.
Complete NERC or utility regulatory compliance packages.

end_to_end_example.scenario_label: Substation event, protection context, and restoration workflow
end_to_end_example.narrative_summary: A substation topology preserves relay, breaker, transformer, control-cabinet, zone, and conduit context so a protective event can be traced into work verification and utility workflow projection without flattening topology into free text.

stages.summary: Utility evidence preserves breaker or relay timing and state context.
Protective events and suppressed alarms remain explicit and governed.
Restoration work and verification remain linked to the substation context.
Zone and conduit context preserves cyber-managed relay and control-cabinet relationships.
A workflow projection can expose outage risk, asset criticality, and related assets without becoming the source of truth.
The example ends with verified restoration context and retained lineage for later review.
